author: David Wildstein
title: Andrew Gross, Murphy's top Israel advisor, will lead AJCs New York office - New Jersey Globe
text:
Andrew Gross, who served as former Gov. Phil Murphy’s point person on Israel, will lead the New York regional office of the American Jewish Committee.
Gross has spent the last several years at the New Jersey Economic Development Authority, most recently as director of international innovation and partnerships. His work focused on bringing foreign investment to New Jersey and developing economic partnerships with other countries.
In 2019, Murphy tapped Gross to run the New Jersey–Israel Commission, which coordinates ties between the state and Israel. Gross handled a portfolio that included business development, education, cultural exchanges, and investment.
Gross came to the Murphy administration with experience in Israeli diplomacy. He previously served as political affairs director at the Israeli consulate in New York, where he worked with elected officials, civic organizations, policy groups and business leaders.
Former Rep. Ted Deutch (D-Florida), the AJC’s CEO, said Gross’ government experience and connections to the Jewish community would be assets as the organization confronts increased antisemitism in New York.
“We are thrilled to welcome Andrew Gross as regional director of AJC New York,” Deutch said. “Andrew brings exceptional leadership, deep community relationships, and a strong commitment to AJC’s mission.”
Gross said he was taking the post at a critical moment for the Jewish community.
“I’m honored to lead AJC’s efforts in the city with the world’s largest Jewish population outside Israel,” Gross said. “At a time when antisemitism has risen to alarming levels in New York and around the world, AJC’s advocacy has never been more needed.”
